IFR-140.e: If any condition is missing, no provision is recognised.
o: There is a present obligation (legal or constructive) from a past event, an outflow is probable and a reliable estimate exists
Operating losses are expected next year
An obligation might arise in the distant future
IFR-140.x:
Basis: IAS 37 – Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets, paragraph 14.
Analysis: Recognise a provision when all hold: a present obligation (legal or constructive) from a past event; a probable (more likely than not) outflow; a reliable estimate. Missing one → no provision (as in VAS 18 – ACC-033).
Distractors: B is earnings management; C – future losses aren't obligations (IFR-142); D isn't a present obligation.

IFR-141.q: Match each situation with its IAS 37 treatment:
IFR-141.e: Contingent assets are disclosed only when an inflow is probable.
p: Present obligation, probable outflow, reliably estimable
IFR-141.x:
Basis: IAS 37.
Analysis: Present obligation, probable outflow, reliable estimate → provision; possible obligation → disclose a contingent liability; virtually certain inflow → no longer contingent, recognise an asset; remote outflow → no disclosure. Contingent assets are disclosed only when an inflow is probable.

IFR-142.q: Provisions may not be recognised for future operating losses.
IFR-142.e: True. Expected losses may indicate a need for asset impairment testing.
IFR-142.x:
Basis: IAS 37, paragraphs 63–65.
Analysis: True. Future operating losses aren't present obligations from past events → no provision. But expected losses signal a need for IAS 36 impairment testing; and onerous contracts do get provisions for their present obligation.

IFR-143.q: Under IAS 21, at period end, foreign-currency monetary items are:
IFR-143.e: Non-monetary items at historical cost keep the transaction-date rate.
o: Translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences in profit or loss
Translated at the annual average rate
IFR-143.x:
Basis: IAS 21 – The effects of changes in foreign exchange rates.
Analysis: At period end, foreign-currency monetary items are translated at the closing rate; differences go to P&L. Non-monetary items at historical cost keep the transaction-date rate; those at fair value use the rate when fair value was measured.
Distractors: B and C are wrong; D – only foreign-operation translation differences go to OCI (IFR-040).
Note: IAS 21 uses one closing rate, without Vietnam's buying/selling split (ACC-068).

IFR-144.q: A supplier payable of USD 10,000 was recorded at 25,000 VND/USD; the closing rate is 26,000. What is the exchange loss (VND million)?
IFR-144.x:
Basis: IAS 21.
Working: FX loss = 10,000 × (26,000 − 25,000) = 10,000,000 VND = 10 million VND (the payable rises as the USD strengthens), to P&L.

IFR-145.q: IFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures, effective 01/01/2027, allows:
IFR-145.e: IFRS 19 reduces disclosures only; recognition and measurement follow full IFRS.
o: Eligible subsidiaries (no public accountability, parent publishes IFRS consolidated FS) to apply reduced disclosures
IFR-145.x:
Basis: IFRS 19 – Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures (IASB, May 2024).
Analysis: IFRS 19, effective 01/01/2027, lets eligible subsidiaries – without public accountability (unlisted, not holding assets in a fiduciary capacity like banks) and with a parent publishing IFRS consolidated FS – apply reduced disclosures. Recognition and measurement remain full IFRS.
Distractors: B, C and D misstate its scope.

IFR-146.q: Under IAS 19, remeasurements of the net defined benefit liability are recognised in OCI and never reclassified to profit or loss.
IFR-146.e: True. Service cost and net interest go to profit or loss.
IFR-146.x:
Basis: IAS 19 – Employee benefits.
Analysis: True. For defined benefit plans: service cost (current and past) and net interest on the net liability/asset go to P&L; remeasurements (actuarial gains and losses, return on plan assets beyond interest) go to OCI and are never reclassified to P&L.

IFR-147.q: A packaged-food company sells via supermarkets allowing returns of near-expiry goods. Under IFRS 15, expected returns are treated as:
IFR-147.e: Estimates are based on historical return data, subject to the constraint.
o: Variable consideration: revenue for goods not expected to be returned, a refund liability and an asset for the right to recover goods
Full revenue, adjusted when returns occur
No revenue until the return period ends
IFR-147.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, Appendix B (B20–B27 – sales with a right of return).
Analysis: The right to return near-expiry goods is variable consideration: revenue for goods not expected back (subject to the constraint – IFR-049); a refund liability for expected returns; an asset for the right to recover goods (cost less recovery costs and expiry impairment). Estimates rest on return history (IFR-061).
Distractors: B overstates revenue; C is over-cautious if estimable; D – it isn't a warranty.

IFR-148.q: A 3-year contract priced at VND 300 million includes a software licence (transferred immediately, standalone price 200) and 3 years of support (standalone price 100). What is year-1 revenue (VND million, 2 decimals)?
IFR-148.e: Licence 200 recognised immediately; support 100 spread over 3 years → 33.33; total 233.33 million VND.
IFR-148.x:
Basis: IFRS 15.
Working: Standalone prices = 200 + 100 = 300 = contract price → no discount to allocate. The licence (right to use – transferred immediately) 200 is recognised in year 1; support 100 straight-line over 3 years → 33.33 a year. Year-1 revenue = 200 + 33.33 = 233.33 million VND.

IFR-149.q: An entity leases a delivery truck for 6 months with no purchase option and elects the short-term exemption. The accounting is:
IFR-149.e: The exemption election is made by class of underlying asset.
o: Expense the rent straight-line (or another systematic basis) over 6 months
Recognise an ROU asset and lease liability
IFR-149.x:
Basis: IFRS 16, paragraph 6 (short-term lease exemption).
Analysis: A 6-month lease with no purchase option, with the exemption elected (by asset class) → expense rent straight-line (or another systematic basis better reflecting the benefit pattern) over 6 months; no ROU asset or liability.
Distractors: B applies if the exemption isn't elected; C – the business doesn't own the truck; D is wrong.

IFR-150.q: A VND 500 million receivable from a struggling distributor (stage 2): lifetime PD 10%, LGD 50%. What is lifetime ECL (VND million)?
IFR-150.x:
Basis: IFRS 9 (lifetime ECL – stage 2).
Working: ECL = EAD × lifetime PD × LGD = 500 × 10% × 50% = 25 million VND (ignoring discounting).
Note: Trade receivables under the simplified approach always use lifetime ECL (IFR-089); 'stage 2' here signals credit risk has risen significantly.

IFR-151.q: Before period end, the entity approved a detailed restructuring plan and announced it to affected employees. Under IAS 37:
IFR-151.e: Announcing a detailed plan creates valid expectations in those affected.
o: Recognise a restructuring provision as a constructive obligation exists
Do not recognise as no cash is paid
IFR-151.x:
Basis: IAS 37, paragraphs 70–83 (restructuring).
Analysis: A constructive restructuring obligation arises with a detailed formal plan (units, locations, headcount, costs, timing) and a valid expectation in those affected (implementation started or main features announced). Both existed before period end → recognise a restructuring provision (direct costs only, excluding retraining, marketing or new systems).
Distractors: B – unpaid cash isn't decisive; C and D are wrong.

IFR-152.q: The board decided to restructure before period end but there is no detailed plan and no announcement. Under IAS 37:
IFR-152.e: An internal decision alone does not create a present obligation.
IFR-152.x:
Basis: IAS 37, paragraph 75.
Analysis: A board decision without a detailed plan or announcement creates no valid expectation in those affected → no constructive obligation at period end → no provision. If announced after period end and material, disclose as a non-adjusting event (IAS 10).
Distractors: B, C and D breach IAS 37.

IFR-153.q: A compressor costs VND 1,000 million: an engine of 200 million (5-year life) and the rest 800 million (20 years); straight-line, no residual value. What is annual depreciation (VND million)?
IFR-153.x:
Basis: IAS 16 (component depreciation).
Working: Engine 200 / 5 = 40 million; remainder 800 / 20 = 40 million. Annual depreciation = 40 + 40 = 80 million VND.
Note: A single 1,000 / 20 = 50 million would understate cost; when the engine is replaced in year 5, the old engine is fully depreciated, avoiding a large disposal loss.

IFR-154.q: Changing depreciation from declining balance to straight-line is a change in accounting estimate applied prospectively.
IFR-154.e: True under IAS 16: the method reflects the expected pattern of consumption of benefits.
IFR-154.x:
Basis: IAS 16, paragraph 61; IAS 8.
Analysis: True. The depreciation method reflects the expected pattern of consuming benefits – an estimate reviewed at least each year end. Changing it (declining balance → straight-line) when the pattern changes is a change in estimate, applied prospectively (IFR-032).

IFR-155.q: Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders is VND 50 billion. Shares outstanding: 8 million for the first half, 12 million for the second half (issued for cash). What is basic EPS (VND)?
IFR-155.e: Weighted average = 8 × 0.5 + 12 × 0.5 = 10 million; EPS = 50 billion / 10 million = 5,000 VND.
IFR-155.x:
Basis: IAS 33.
Working: Weighted average shares = 8 × 6/12 + 12 × 6/12 = 4 + 6 = 10 million. Basic EPS = 50,000 million / 10 million = 5,000 VND per share.
Note: Using 12 million year-end shares gives 4,167 – wrong (cf. ACC-130).

IFR-156.q: A Vietnamese subsidiary sells mainly in USD at international market prices and incurs mostly USD costs. Under IAS 21, its functional currency:
IFR-156.e: Functional currency follows the primary economic environment, not the country of registration.
o: May be USD, as the currency mainly influencing prices and costs
Must be VND because it operates in Vietnam
IFR-156.x:
Basis: IAS 21, paragraphs 9–12 (functional currency).
Analysis: The functional currency is that of the primary economic environment – mainly influencing sales prices (often the pricing and settlement currency) and labour and material costs. With sales and costs mainly in USD and prices set internationally → the functional currency may be USD.
Distractors: B – not by country of registration; C – not the parent's free choice; D has no basis.
Note: FS filed in Vietnam must still be translated into VND (ACC-005, ACC-020).

IFR-157.q: On first-time IFRS adoption, an entity has goodwill being amortised under Vietnamese rules. Under IFRS 1's business combinations exemption, it may:
IFR-157.e: From transition, goodwill is no longer amortised; it is tested for impairment under IAS 36.
o: Not restate past combinations under IFRS 3, keep the previous-GAAP goodwill carrying amount at transition and test it for impairment
IFR-157.x:
Basis: IFRS 1, Appendix C (business combinations exemption); IFRS 3; IAS 36.
Analysis: First-time adopters may skip retrospective IFRS 3 for pre-transition combinations: keep goodwill's previous-GAAP carrying amount at the transition date (after specific adjustments) and test it for impairment then. From the transition date there's no amortisation; annual IAS 36 testing applies.
Distractors: B and D have no basis; C breaches IFRS 3.

IFR-158.q: During the period 20 young animals are born on a livestock farm, with fair value less costs to sell of VND 5 million each. What gain is recognised on initial recognition of the biological assets (VND million)?
IFR-158.e: 20 × 5 = 100 million VND recognised in profit or loss under IAS 41.
IFR-158.x:
Basis: IAS 41, paragraph 28.
Working: Gain on initial recognition of biological assets (newborn animals) = 20 × 5 = 100 million VND, to P&L in the period.
Note: Under VAS (no IAS 41 equivalent), newborns are usually recorded at cost with no gain at birth – a major conversion difference for livestock firms.

IFR-159.q: Consider these IFRS 15 statements for a fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company selling through distributors and supermarkets:
IFR-159.e: Taxes collected on behalf are not revenue; consignment revenue arises when control passes to the end customer.
o: Volume rebates are variable consideration reducing revenue.
Listing fees paid to supermarkets (customers) reduce revenue unless in exchange for a distinct service.
Taxes collected for the State are included in revenue.
Consignment goods are recognised as revenue on delivery to the consignee.
IFR-159.x:
Basis: IFRS 15.
Analysis: True: volume rebates are variable consideration reducing revenue (estimated by a suitable method – IFR-048); display fees paid to supermarkets (customers) reduce revenue unless for a distinct service with measurable fair value. False: taxes collected for the State (VAT, excise collected on its behalf) aren't revenue (ACC-042); consignment goods are revenue only when control passes to the end customer (the agent sells).

IFR-160.q: Under IFRS, if there is no indication of impairment, goodwill need not be tested.
IFR-160.e: False. Goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles must be tested annually.
IFR-160.x:
Basis: IAS 36, paragraph 10.
Analysis: False. Regardless of indicators, annual impairment tests are required for: goodwill; indefinite-life intangibles; intangibles not yet available for use. Other assets are tested only when there are indicators (IFR-114).
